newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Battle Mountain Q3 loss US$49 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Battle Mountain Q3 loss US$49 mln.

text.p: Battle Mountain Gold Co (BMG) reported on Friday a third quarter 1996 consolidated net loss of US$49 million, or 21 cents per share.
The third quarter loss compares with a net loss of $0.8 million in the same period last year.
For the nine months, consolidated net loss was $42.3 million or 18 cents per share, compared with net income of $22.3 million or 10 cents per share, in the same period in 1995, BMG said.
The Houston-based miner released the results to the Australian Stock Exchange, where its shares are also listed.
The results are the first since the merger with Hemlo Gold Mines and include total before tax charges of $19.2 million for merger related costs, and asset write-downs of $38.5 million.
BMG Chairman Karl E. Elers said in a statement the merger related costs were required to be recognised as a one time, current expense under pooling of interests accounting rules.
Under these accounting principles, future earnings will not be burdened by amortisation of these costs, nor goodwill which would have arisen had the merger, Elers said.

Elers said the asset write downs were a result of the current review of the company's business which resulted in recognising the inability to recover the carrying values of certain assets under U.S. accounting guidelines.
He said the enlarged BMG was completing the merger process and establishing a new way of doing business.
He added the company was establishing a firm base from which it will grow through operational efficiencies, exploration and value-adding acquisitions.
BMG will be supported in those activities by its strong balance sheet and considerable financial flexibility, he said.
